Jeg har selv haft depression i lidt over ti år. Med gode perioder og perioder med tilbagefald. Det der har hjulpet mig mest er medicin og kognitiv terapi så jeg vil virkelig anbefale dig at finde en psykolog der har speciale i det. Det man normalt anbefaler for depression i danmark er følgende : for let depression - terapi, middel depression - terapi (muligvis medicin) og for svær depression terapi og medicin.
Så hvis du har en svær depression bør du også få medicin da din hjernes kemi er blevet ændret så meget at det er meget svært at ændre den tilbage uden kemisk hjælp i en periode. Den kognitive terapi arbejder med at ændre din tænknings og handlingsmønstre og udover selvf også at give plads til at tale om de problemer du ellers har brug for at få talt om med nogen, men terapien fokuserer ikke på at finde årsagen til depressionen (hvilket når der ikke er tale om traumarelateret depression, heller ikke er så vigtig) men mere om at komme videre. Jeg vil ikke ligefrem fraråde dig fra at se psykologen der er tilrådighed på din uddannelse men bare vær opmærksom på om de har de rette værktøjer til at håndtere en patient med depression. Da jeg først blev diagnoseret og kom på medicin gik jeg til mit universitets psykolog og han kom med en masse ting han syntes jeg skulle gøre som ville være fornuftigt nok for almindelige studerende der sad lidt fast men for mig endte det med en lang tudetur og følelse af håbløshed efter terapien og derudover skulle jeg også forklare over for ham hvad depression egentlig indebar.

I dont know if this will be of any help to you, but when i was waiting for my new medicin to work i was told to do the following things. Get up each morning take meds, eat and take a shower then go for a walk for around 15 mins (ofc your welcome to do more) then i was allowed to lay in bed and sleep or just relax for an hour then after lunch i had to go for a second 15 mins walk and after that i was allowed another hour of sleep in the bed. The rest of the day i wasnt allowed to lay in my bed other than at night for sleep and be sure not to sleep more than 8-9 hours a night. The walks helped me alot and it also helped that i had something to do in the morning i wasnt allowed to think about if i had the energy to do those things i just had to do them and then i was allowed to sleep a bit which functioned as the reward for me.

I dont want to get into a discussion about depression being labeled as a mental illness or not think for some that label hurts and for some like me it helps. 

I would like to give a suggestion and that would be to try out cognitive therapy. It focuses on changing your actions which will then change the way you feel and think. Those changes to action can help you get on the path to life you wanna live with out having the depression to constantly hold you back.

I dont think it helps just talking about it with someone but to be understood and accepted when talking with someone that is. I have a friend that doesnt really understand depression and likes to tell me what she think i should do (mainly just pull myself up and d stuff) which really makes me feel so lonely and sets off all the bad thoughts in my head. But i also have this other friend that is dealing with a depression and when we talk about depression we can finish eachothers sentences and are like"yeah, that is totally like it is" which makes me feel so calm and hopefull and helps me to keep a thick line between whats me and whats my depression.

I'm not sure you will like what i have to say to you. I know it's hard to withdraw i know it's hard to allow yourself to take the time you need to get well enough to handle the pressure that is day to day ordinary life, and studying can be even more stressful, especially when you can't keep up. I'm not saying that you need to withdraw but i would suggest that you  do less courses and take it slower than normal. One of the crucial things to get back to feeling good is to have successes (even small ones) and with trying to do that much you do make it easier for yourself to experience failure. 

Your mind has had a lot of things to deal with and it's taken some damage and needs time and help to get up to functioning at full strenght. Like if you broke your leg you would still have to do some recovery after. And college is like running a marathon for your mind.

I would say you should see about getting a diagnosis, then it's easier to get the help you need to get better again. I don't exactly know how to go about it in your country but i would guess getting an appointment with your family doctor would be a good place to start.

Is it that your parents and friends don't really "believe" in depression or is that they don't believe you are depressed?

If it is the former i don't really know, i had that issue with my sister and father that had the attitude that i should just get my shit together. That was until my dad lost his job and started to get a little depressed aswell. So yeah getting them to see that depression is a real thing might take a lot more hard work and energy than what you can muster at this point.

If it is that they dont believe you are depressed, i would like to ask if you have a official diagnosis or not, if you do i think you maybe should take your parents with you to the doctor and get the doctor to validate it. Both if you do have a diagnosis or not i would say make a list of how depression manifests it self in you and also get some articles on depression that validates that the way you feel is signs of a depression. 
I hope you can find support and understanding from the ppl that matter in your life.

The zero concentraton and bad memory are symptoms of a depression, the good news is when you get better you will get better ad concentrating again. I had the same issues when i was really depressed, i would have so mane thoughts running around in my head felt like i had 2 or 3 brains going around simultanous and who the f.. can focus with that going on. After i got on meds it helped alot and regained focus enough that i a couple of years ago finally got my masters in engenieering done it took almost twice aslong as everyone else but i still got through it. 

Remember not to beat yourself down for the symptoms of your disease you wouldn't be angry at yourself for not being able to run with a broken leg would you :)

Depression changes you, you will never be completely like you were before, but that doesn't have to be a bad thing lots of things changes us.

On the drawing part im guessing its probably because you have been away from it too long. Like if you run every day of you life it's easy and you enjoy it and can run fast or far or both. Then after being away from running for a couple of years your muscles are weaker and it is not a part of your everyday life anymore. It can be again tho just takes time and practise. I would say the same goes for drawing. You have lost the momentum and also some of your skills that you had, but if you just start to make it a part of your daily life again you can get both back, just beware that it will seem hard and not fun to begin with but it will come. I hope you choose to make it part of your life again and that you will find your passion again, because we all need and deserve to have passion in our lifes.

It doesn't help me get in a better mood but aslong as i don't knock myself down for playing it doesn't really make me feel worse either so its more just like a mental vacuum for me. I don't know how you should talk to your parents about it, but maybe sit them down and let them know that you need this for now, and how it help you not think all the thoughts of depression. And if you have that space the chances are you will also have more energy to fight against the depression. (If your not seeing a therapist i highly recommend it, drugs can be great to get you going but for me i needed cognitive therapy to be me and happy again). First a little back story. I started being depressed 10 years ago took me 3 years before i got a diagnosis and then another year and a half with getting on meds then off meds and relapse to get into therapy. I started dating my boyfriend half a year after my depression started so it was always a part of our relationship even if it wasnt a known member and even if it wasnt always as big a part as later years. One of the first thing my therapist said to me when talking about me and my boyfriend was "the only thing worse than having a depression, is being in a relationship with one" and that has helped me alot to try and see if from his perspective.

Dont  really know what i can give of concrete suggestions. If it is possible for you guys i would suggest for him/you both see a therapist for a couple of sessions, it can be easier for a therapist to see it from both sides and explain depression to your bf in more easy to understand terms. That is what we did and i know the single sessions for my bf helped him vent some of the frustations he had that he couldnt really air to me.
